d: File .git/objects/info/alternates listing paths to shared object stores; enables disk-space savings across clones.
PGP signature stored within tag object body; verified by git tag -v; authenticates the tagged object SHA-1.
Composite of author_timestamp and author_timezone; git log --date= formats this value.
String component of the author field in a commit object specifying the primary creator's email address; appears in angle brackets after the name in the standard <name> <email> format.
Name and email in commit object identifying primary creator; distinct from committer who applied the patch.
Full author identity string in the form 'Name <email> timestamp timezone_offset' embedded in a commit object's author header; the canonical representation of author_field.
The combination of author_name and author_email forming the author's identity within the commit object.
String component of the author field in a commit object specifying the primary creator's display name; appears before the email in the standard <name> <email> format.
The RFC 2822 formatted author line: "author <name> <email> <timestamp> <timezone>" stored in commit object body.
Integer Unix timestamp recording when the author created the change; represents seconds since epoch (1970-01-01 00:00:00 UTC) in the author field.
String timezone offset in the author field following the timestamp; formatted as +HHMM or -HHMM indicating hours and minutes east or west of UTC.
The semantic distinction: author created the patch content; committer applied it to the repository; git blame uses author_field as the primary attribution.
refs/bisect/* pseudo-refs tracking midpoints and test results during git bisect; --no-checkout mode walks history without checkout.
Type-1 git object storing raw file contents verbatim; identified by SHA-1 of content; no filename or metadata retained.
Git fetch-object or protocol v2 advertisements retrieving missing blob content on demand from partial clone; requires server support.
Configuration core.bigFileThreshold beyond which git may store deltas instead of full content in packfiles.
Commit-graph embedded data structure encoding paths modified per commit; powers git log --S <string> --throughput optimization.
Remote-tracking ref establishing upstream relationship; configured via branch.<name>.remote and branch.<name>.merge; used for push.default and @{upstream}.
Self-contained .git-bundle file encoding ref updates and reachable objects; enables offline transfer via removable media.
The raw byte sequence forming the name; git stores no encoding assumption, no null bytes permitted within the name itself, and no guaranteed UTF-8 validity.

The name bytes are stored verbatim and compared byte-for-byte, making the entry case-sensitive on all operating systems including case-insensitive filesystems where the working tree normalizes casing.
Apply single commit's diff as new commit; preserves original author; generates new SHA-1; records original SHA-1 in commit message.
Configured program git attributes runs on git checkout; transforms blob from object store before writing to working tree.
Revision list ordering by commit timestamp; --date-order flag; faster than topological but produces non-ancestor-first sequences.
Revision traversal predicate (--since, --author, --grep, --S, --G) restricting which commits appear in output.
Binary file .git/objects/info/commit-graph storing commit reachability, generation numbers, and bloom filter data off the critical path.
git commit-graph verify reads graph and validates generation numbers, checksum, and fanout structure; reports corruption.
git commit-graph write traverses reachable commits and writes binary graph; --split merges small chains; --append adds commits to existing graph.
Commit object may record encoding header; git log --encoding=UTF-8 transcodes as needed; enables non-ASCII commit messages.
The terminal or output stream encoding git uses when writing the transcoded_message; git assumes UTF-8 output if terminal encoding is unset.
State when a commit object lacks an encoding header; git treats the message as UTF-8 by default per the unicode interpretation rule.
Fallback behavior when transcoding_logic cannot map a character; typically replaces with a substitution character or skips the byte.
Optional header line 'encoding <encoding-name>' in a commit object's raw text; git stores whatever the user wrote verbatim.
The character encoding name stored in the encoding header (UTF-8, ISO-8859-1, Windows-1252, etc.); controls byte-to-character interpretation of the message bytes.
git log flag --encoding=<enc> specifying the target encoding for transcoded output; overrides the stored encoding for display purposes.
Raw byte sequence forming the commit message body; decoded using encoding_value (or assumed UTF-8) to produce display characters.
Alias for encoding_value; the encoding recorded at commit time distinguishing the message's original byte interpretation from the display encoding.
The output of transcoding_logic: message_bytes decoded then re-encoded into log_encoding_flag; git log emits this to the terminal.
git's internal conversion from the stored encoding_value to the requested log_encoding_flag encoding; uses iconv-style conversion with loss handling.
Type-3 git object containing tree SHA, parent SHA(s), author, committer, timestamp, and message; forms the history DAG backbone.
Name, email, timestamp, and timezone offset in commit object; records who committed (not necessarily who authored).
Full committer identity string in form 'Name <email> timestamp timezone_offset' in the commit object; distinct from author_ident.
Integer -1 (zlib default), 0 (store), 1-9 (fast to best); set via core.compression or per-object pack-objects --compression.
Property that object identity derives solely from its content hash; same content always yields identical identifier regardless of path or history.
Packfile command copying bytes from base object at offset+length; encodes file copy without recompression.
Checksum stored per object in packfile index; verified on read to detect corruption before decompression.
Alternative backend via GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY or extensions.objectFormat; allows SHA-256, shared storage, or plugin-based stores.
Blob object with no parent tree entry; arises from aborted rebase or staged-but-uncommitted content; harmless but obscures analysis.
Git's storage optimization encoding an object as a series of copy/insert commands relative to a base object; OFS_DELTA uses relative offsets; REF_DELTA uses absolute SHA-1.
Packfile grouping mechanism isolating objects reachable via specific refs; prevents cross-island delta sharing; aids monorepo incremental fetch.
The rule that a tree entry name cannot contain an internal null byte because null is the field terminator; any such byte would truncate the name prematurely.
SHA-1 of the empty tree (tree with zero entries): 4b825dc642cb6eb9a060e54bf8d69288fbee4904; used as synthetic parent of root commits.
Mode 100755; regular file with execute bits set; Git marks it this way to preserve the executable bit across platforms that handle it differently.
Temporary .git/FETCH_HEAD file recording all branches fetched and their merge configuration for the next pull operation.
The octet value 0x2F representing the ASCII forward slash character; signals subdirectory boundary in tree entry name byte sequences.
git fsck traverses all reachable objects validating SHA-1 linkage, ref integrity, and accessibility; reports dangling and unreachable.
System call flushing object file to durable storage; controlled by core.fsyncObjectFiles; trades safety against write throughput.
Garbage collection process expunging unreachable objects older than prune.window; configurable via gc.prune expire and git prune.
Integer in commit-graph measuring topological distance from roots; enables fast ancestor queries without traversing full commit history.
File .git/info/grafts (or .git/shallow) overriding or truncating commit ancestry; used for repository imports with incomplete history.
Commit referenced by a branch tip; all ancestors reachable; descendant commits unreferenced subject to gc if no other path retains them.
Flag hash --write causes git to store the computed object in .git/objects/ after hashing; idempotent on repeat.
Symbolic ref .git/HEAD pointing to current branch name or directly to a SHA-1 in detached mode; moves on checkout.
Namespace .git/refs/heads/ containing local branch references; each file = branch name; its SHA-1 = tip commit.
Environment variables (GIT_DIR, GIT_WORK_TREE, GIT_QUARANTINE_PATH) passed to hook executables; quarantine prevents bad objects from entering repo.
Executable script under .git/hooks/ invoked by specific git commands (pre-commit, post-commit, pre-rebase, etc.); nonzero exit aborts operation.
Binary staging area at .git/index listing path->blob SHA-1 mappings plus stage numbers for unmerged entries; fast diff vs tree computation.
Packfile command appending literal byte sequence to output; the raw new content not derivable from base.
Git's default rebase behavior assumes first parent path is mainline; git log --first-parent exposes linearized view; bisect follows first parent.
Individual compressed file stored at .git/objects/xx/xxxx...; fast to write but inefficient at scale; one object per file.
Background git maintenance --scheduled running via cron or systemd timer; config thresholds in maintenance.<task>.schedule.
git maintenance subcommand scheduling background optimization: gc, commit-graph rebuild, incremental-repack, prefetch, prune.
拜占庭容错特性: tree SHA derived from entry hashes and names; any content change ripples upward; enables tamper-evident history without full content comparison.
Base-8 positional numeral system used to encode file mode; Git stores exactly 6 octal digits representing 18 bits of mode information.
The lower 9 bits (three octal digits) encoding Unix owner/group/other read-write-execute permissions; displayed as the last three digits of the 6-digit octal mode.
The upper bits of the octal mode identifying the entry's object category: regular file, directory, symlink, or submodule; encoded in the first two octal digits.
The leading zero in modes like 100644 and 040000 ensures consistent 6-digit width; the zero fills the third octal digit reserved for special file type flags.
Compound .midx file spanning multiple packfiles; enables cross-pack object queries and accelerates repack scenarios.
Practical limits on tree entry name bytes derived from path length limits and the 4096-byte tree object ceiling; individual names cannot contain embedded null bytes.
Blob-like object linked via refs/notes/commits/ to commits; provides annotation layer outside normal commit history.
The terminal byte value 0x00 that marks the boundary between a tree entry name and the following field (mode space or next entry) in the binary tree object format.
The rule that a null byte (0x00) terminates the tree entry name field, separating it from the following mode and SHA-1 blob reference within the tree entry binary structure.
Directory-backed key-value store under .git/objects/; loose objects stored as zlib-deflated files keyed by SHA-1; packed objects aggregated into packfiles.
Count of loose objects in .git/objects subdirs; high count triggers automatic gc; git count-objects reports count and size.
Four-byte prefix of every loose object: type byte + space + decimal size + null byte before payload; enables streaming deserialization.
git cat-file -t reveals object type; git cat-file -s shows byte size; git cat-file -p pretty-prints content; git rev-list walks commit graph.
A single 8-bit byte serving as the atomic encoding unit within a tree entry name byte string; Git stores names as raw bytes with no character encoding assumption.
Merge commit with more than two parents; octopus strategy combines multiple branches; refs/heads/main lists all parents in merge commit object.
Merge strategy handling 3+ branch tips simultaneously; creates single commit with all parents; avoids intermediate pairwise merges.
Delta format encoding base object as relative offset within packfile; safer for streaming than REF_DELTA which names base by SHA-1.
Merge strategy favoring current branch content for conflicts; creates new commit with all parents but discards theirs content.
Maximum delta chain length before stopping; deeper chains improve compression but slow random access; default 50.
Consolidated .git/packed-refs file containing refs not in loose format; created by git pack-refs; enables faster startup on repos with many refs.
Single binary file consolidating many objects via delta compression; named pack-*.pack with companion .idx index; vastly reduces repository size.
Reachability bitmap at packfile end enabling fast network transfer negotiation and clone/fetch optimization by marking all reachable objects.
Binary lookup table (.idx) enabling O(log n) SHA-1 to offset resolution within a packfile; also stores CRC-32 for integrity verification.
Smart protocol phase where server advertises reachable refs and client computes minimum packfile of missing objects using haves/wants.
Comma-separated list of parent SHA-1s in commit object; first parent first enables linear history heuristics; octopush uses multi-parent.
Clone with --filter omitting blob objects from transfer; missing blobs retrieved on demand via fetch-object; enables huge-repository workflows.
Conceptual role: the person who originally wrote the code change; represented by author_ident in the commit object.
The derivation of individual directory components by splitting the name on forward slash boundaries, producing the hierarchical path representation git reconstructs.
The forward slash character (0x2F) embedded within the name byte string signals a directory boundary; git parses no actual directory structure, only the slash as a naming convention.

The mismatch where the stored tree entry name bytes are compared literally but the host filesystem may fold case on lookup, causing apparent mismatches resolved by Git's case-insensitive matching logic.
Reference in a partial clone marking an object as promised but not yet fetched; enables placeholder usage before physical retrieval.
Property of an object being transitively accessible from another; defines ancestry in the commit DAG; basis for gc, merge-base, and history queries.
Replay commits as new objects onto new base; each original commit replaced; original SHA-1s abandoned; creates new history branch.
Merge strategy recursing into trees for three-way content merge; handles rename detection and conflict presentation.
Virtual filesystem layer for ref storage; files backend for loose refs, reftable backend for high-scale; configured via extensions.refStorage.
Delta format referencing base object by its SHA-1; simpler but requires base to precede delta in packfile or be separately reachable.
Named file under .git/refs/ containing a SHA-1; represents a branch tip, tag, or remote-tracking branch; updated atomically during operations.
Atomic multi-ref update mechanism; all-or-nothing semantics; used by git update-ref --transaction for safe concurrent modifications.
Append-only log at .git/logs/ tracking all ref changes with old SHA, new SHA, timestamp, and actor; enables recovery from accidental resets or branch deletions.
Pattern mapping source to destination ref during fetch/push: [+]<src>:<dst>; enables selective branch transfer and namespace rewriting.
Binary sorted table format for refs replacing loose files + packed-refs; compact, concurrent-writer-safe; default for repositories over 1GB.
Mode 100644; standard blob-backed file with read permission for all and write for owner; the default for non-executable files committed to Git.
Ref update in refs/remotes/ namespace during fetch; controlled by remote.<name>.fetch config; default +refs/heads/*:refs/remotes/origin/*.
Namespace .git/refs/remotes/ containing remote-tracking branches; updated by fetch, not by user edits; represent server state.
Reference under refs/replace/ mapping an object SHA to a substitute SHA; transparent to most commands; allows history rewriting without modifying history.
Extended reference syntax: HEAD~n (n-th ancestor), HEAD^n (n-th parent in merge), HEAD@{n} (reflog entry), HEAD^{type} (dereference type).
Revision traversal with --reverse flag; emits commits from oldest to newest; useful for generating forward history scripts.
Generate commit whose tree undoes another commit's changes; opposite of cherry-pick; uses three-way merge to compute inverse patch.

An ordered walk over commits in git's object graph, visiting each revision reachable from one or more starting points (refs, commits) following parent links, in depth-first, breadth-first, or topological order, to collect metadata, compute reachability, or stream objects for processing.
Commit with zero parent SHAs; git mktree produces empty tree SHA; git rev-list excludes root commits with --max-parents=0 when negating.
Property that finding two distinct contents with same SHA-1 requires ~2^80 operations; git relies on this for object identity.
160-bit cryptographic hash computed over object content; serves as object's unique addressable name in git's content-addressable store.
Gradual transition from SHA-1 to SHA-256 object names; support for SHA-256-only repositories since git 2.29; object format stored in config.
Clone with .git/shallow cut-off file listing shallow commit SHAs; prevents fetching ancestors beyond the boundary.
Commit with GPGSIG header containing cryptographic signature over commit contents; verified by git verify-commit.
Configured program git attributes runs on git add; transforms working-tree file before storing as object; lazy loading via .gitattributes.
Remove stash entry; objects remain reachable via reflog until reflog expiry; --index flag restores staged state from stash commit tree.
Pseudo-branch at refs/stash maintained by git stash; each stash entry is a commit whose tree captures working-directory state.
The portion of a tree entry name between forward slash bytes; corresponds to a single directory level in the repository path hierarchy.
Entry in a parent repository's tree object referencing a specific commit of a nested repository; stored as mode 160000 with commit SHA-1.
Merge strategy handling repository-in-repository layout; subtrees/ subcommand maintains synthetic history linking project roots.
Mode 040000; entry points to a nested tree object representing a directory; the tree entry name contains a forward slash but the slash is not stored in the entry itself.
Merge variant treating branch tip trees as subtrees of current tree; read-tree + commit without losing either branch's subdirectory content.
Mode 120000; entry points to a blob object containing the target path as raw bytes; the blob content is the symlink destination, not the link data itself.
Type-4 git object wrapping another object with a tag name, tagger info, and message; typically used for annotated release markers.
Namespace .git/refs/tags/ containing tag references; may point directly at commits (lightweight) or at tag objects (annotated).
Revision list ordering guaranteeing all parents precede children; --topo-order flag; required for linearized history display.
GIT_TRACE_PACKET, GIT_TRACE_PERFORMANCE, GIT_TRACE_SETUP, GIT_TRACE_OID logging to stderr; GIT_TRACE2 structured event output for tooling.
Wire format for git fetch/push; smart protocol negotiates packfile contents; dumb protocol requires static file serving of .git/objects/.

A fixed-format record within a Git tree object containing an octal mode, a space separator, a null-terminated name, a space, a 20-byte SHA-1 reference, and a newline; entries are sorted lexicographically by their tree_entry_name byte sequence.
Octal mode in tree object: 100644 (regular file), 100755 (executable), 040000 (subtree), 120000 (symlink), 160000 (submodule).
Null-terminated byte string within tree entry; may contain slash for subdirectory entries; case-sensitive on all platforms.
The property that tree_entry_name_raw_bytes preserve exact byte case from the moment of entry; git never folds case to a canonical form during storage.

The property that git performs byte-exact comparison of tree entry names during lookup and merge; names differing only in case are distinct entries on all platforms including macOS HFS+ and NTFS (which are case-preserving but case-insensitive at the OS layer).
Tree entry names equal to . or .. which git handles as special directory references in index operations; the raw bytes are stored verbatim with no transformation.

The period byte (0x2E) that may appear within the name to separate basename from extension; git makes no special interpretation of this byte — it is ordinary content unless it is the leading byte of .. or . special entries.
The byte offset of the rightmost slash byte within the name; everything after this index is the filename portion, everything before (including any preceding slash) is the directory portion.
The byte count of tree_entry_name_raw_bytes; git computes this from the offset between the space after mode and the null terminator during parsing.
A tree_entry_name containing one or more slash bytes — represents a file at arbitrary depth; git stores the full relative path string as a single null-terminated name field.
The single NUL byte (0x00) that delimits the end of the tree entry name field; git parses tree objects by scanning for this byte to extract the name string from the mode-space-name-null-SHA sequence.

The exact byte sequence stored between the space after mode and the NUL terminator; git treats these bytes as opaque — no encoding interpretation, no normalization, no validation of valid filesystem characters.
A tree_entry_name with no slash byte — represents a file directly in the containing directory; the name bytes constitute the full filename without path prefix.
The forward-slash byte (0x2F) that may appear anywhere within tree_entry_name_raw_bytes to indicate subdirectory hierarchy; git stores the slash literally without encoding or escaping.
A common case where tree_entry_name_raw_bytes form a valid UTF-8 encoded string representing a human-readable filename; git stores the raw bytes without validating or re-encoding them.
Type-2 git object listing directory entries as (mode, name, sha1) tuples; represents a single directory snapshot at a point in time.
Object with valid content but no reference path from any ref, reflog entry, or other reachable object; candidate for garbage collection.
git worktree list enumerates all linked working trees sharing one object store and refs; main worktree distinguished by gitdir file location.
File .git/worktrees/<name>/HEAD and GITDIR files linking a linked working tree to the main repository's object store and refs.
Deflate compression applied to all loose object content and packfile entries; balance of speed and ratio; configurable per object type via core.compression.
